text: Seventy-two clubs from 48 countries entered the Champions League in July; 32 reached the group stage in September.
Old Trafford averaged 67,641 a game, four times the crowd Fulham drew at Loftus Road.
Until Christmas, first and third in the Premier League were never more than five points apart.
Liverpool took more league shots than anyone, 558, and finished 30 points behind Arsenal.
Monaco beat Deportivo 8-3 in the group stage, and Deportivo still reached the semi-finals.
At halfway four points covered the top three, with Manchester United first; by May it was fifteen and United were third.
Porto, the eventual champions, came through their group second, three points behind Real Madrid.
United took 2.27 points a game before Rio Ferdinand's eight-month ban began on 20 January and 1.56 after it.

text: Six clubs led the Premier League in 2003-04, the lead changed hands 20 times, and after 1 February only Arsenal led.
February was the season's highest-scoring month at 3.21 goals a game, and in March home sides won 22 of 34.
English clubs won three of the eight Champions League groups and none of them reached the final.
teams: Arsenal, Chelsea, Manchester United, Newcastle United

text: Thierry Henry scored 30 league goals from 23.9 expected, seven of them in eight days of April.
Two quarter-finals turned in the second leg, Deportivo from 4-1 down against the holders Milan and Monaco from 4-2 down against Real Madrid.
teams: Deportivo La Coruña, AC Milan, Monaco, Real Madrid

text: Monaco had the competition's two top scorers, Fernando Morientes with nine and Dado Pršo with seven.

text: Porto won the final 3-0 with four shots worth 0.50 expected goals.
Porto lost once in thirteen Champions League games; Monaco lost four times and still reached the final.
Seven days after the final, Porto's José Mourinho became Chelsea manager.
Home sides won 167 of the 380 league games, and nobody beat Arsenal home or away.
Arsenal took 14 more points than the bookmakers' prices implied and Manchester City about 10 fewer.
Portugal sent two clubs to the Champions League and one of them won it.
Eight of the fifteen knockout ties were settled by one goal or on away goals, and Monaco went through twice on away goals.
